study_name.notes: No canonical study name/acronym is given in the text; the paper is referred to only by its full title.

subject_id.notes: Only donor codes (Donor 1-6) and patient counts (n=23, n=17, n=30) are reported; no per-subject ID table is present in the provided text.

sample_id.notes: Sample-level identifiers are only referenced indirectly via Supplementary Tables (S1A, S2A) which are not included in the provided text.

pmid.notes: PMID not stated within the paper text itself.

subcohort.notes: Multiple sub-populations exist (Donor 1 healthy control, Donor 2/3 treatment-naive RA, NORA cohort n=23, MTX-R n=8, MTX-NR n=15) but no single 'subcohort' label is defined uniformly across the paper.

target_condition.evidence_quote: Methotrexate (MTX), a first-line rheumatoid arthritis (RA) treatment, inhibits mammalian dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR)
target_condition.notes: Healthy donor (Donor 1) samples were also used as controls for gnotobiotic mouse experiments, but the overarching clinical condition studied is RA.

control.evidence_quote: Consecutive patients from the New York University Langone Medical Center's rheumatology clinics and offices were screened for the presence of RA
control.section: STAR Methods — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition
control.notes: The main human clinical cohort consists of RA patients (cases); a separate healthy male donor (Donor 1) was used only as a stool source for gnotobiotic mouse colonization, not as a clinical control subject with matched metadata.

country.evidence_quote: Consecutive patients from the New York University Langone Medical Center's rheumatology clinics and offices were screened
country.section: STAR Methods — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition
country.notes: Country not explicitly stated; inferred from NYU Langone Medical Center location.

body_site.evidence_quote: DNA was extracted from human fecal samples (n=23 patients, 46 stool samples)
body_site.section: STAR Methods — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition

days_from_first_collection.evidence_quote: Stool samples were collected at baseline and 1 month after MTX initiation
days_from_first_collection.section: Results — Clinical relevance of the interaction between methotrexate and the human gut microbiome
days_from_first_collection.notes: Longitudinal timepoints (baseline, 1 month) reported but no single study-level day offset value applies; this is a per-sample attribute not extractable as one value.

location.value: New York University Langone Medical Center
location.evidence_quote: Consecutive patients from the New York University Langone Medical Center's rheumatology clinics and offices were screened
location.section: STAR Methods — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition

antibiotics_exclusion_period.evidence_quote: recent (<3 months prior) use of any antibiotic therapy
antibiotics_exclusion_period.section: STAR Methods — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition
antibiotics_exclusion_period.notes: Reported as an exclusion criterion (patients excluded if antibiotic use occurred within 3 months).

antibiotics_exclusion_period_unit.evidence_quote: recent (<3 months prior) use of any antibiotic therapy
antibiotics_exclusion_period_unit.section: STAR Methods — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition

dna_extraction_kit.evidence_quote: using the MoBio Powersoil DNA extraction kit, based on cell membrane disruption by high-speed shaking
dna_extraction_kit.section: STAR Methods — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition
dna_extraction_kit.notes: Other sample sets (gnotobiotic mouse, RA metagenomics) used ZymoBIOMICS 96 MagBead DNA Kit; kit choice varies by sample subset.

ncbi_accession.evidence_quote: All sequencing data generated in the preparation of this manuscript has been deposited in NCBI's Sequence Read Archive (SRA), under Bioproject ID PRJNA656577.

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: was performed using a MiSeq Illumina platform (150-bp read length, paired-end protocol) at the New York University Genome Technology Center
sequencing_platform.section: STAR Methods — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition
sequencing_platform.notes: Shotgun metagenomic sequencing of the same RA cohort used NovaSeq ('pooled for sequencing on the NovaSeq using S1 or S2 platform'); platform varies by assay type.

age.notes: Only an eligibility threshold (age 18 years or older) is given, not actual participant ages.

age_group.evidence_quote: all subjects be age 18 years or older
age_group.section: STAR Methods — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition
age_group.notes: Only a minimum age eligibility criterion is given; actual age distribution not reported, so a definitive age_group cannot be assigned.

sex.evidence_quote: a treatment-naïve (re-MTX) female and male donors with rheumatoid arthritis
sex.notes: Both male (Donor 1, healthy) and mixed female/male RA donors are described; no single sex value applies to the overall NYU RA cohort in the provided text.

zigosity.notes: No twin study or zygosity information present in this paper.

age_min.evidence_quote: that all subjects be age 18 years or older
age_min.section: STAR METHODS — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition
age_min.notes: This is an inclusion criterion (minimum age), not a specific cohort mean/median age; no maximum age reported.

age_max.notes: No upper age bound reported for human RA patients.

age_years.notes: No specific mean/median age reported for the human RA cohort in the main text.

antibiotics_current_use.evidence_quote: recent (<3 months prior) use of any antibiotic therapy
antibiotics_current_use.section: STAR METHODS — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition
antibiotics_current_use.notes: Derived from exclusion criteria: patients with recent (<3 months) antibiotic use were excluded, implying enrolled patients were not currently on antibiotics.

bmi.notes: BMI not reported in the paper.

dietary_restriction.evidence_quote: current extreme diet (e.g., parenteral nutrition or macrobiotic diet)
dietary_restriction.section: STAR METHODS — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition
dietary_restriction.notes: This is only an exclusion criterion (patients with extreme diets were excluded), not a positive dietary restriction reported for included participants.

disease.evidence_quote: Consecutive patients from the New York University Langone Medical Center's rheumatology clinics and offices were screened for the presence of RA based on ACR criteria
disease.section: STAR METHODS — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition

disease_details.evidence_quote: New-onset RA was defined as disease duration of a minimum of 6 weeks and up to 6 months since diagnosis
disease_details.section: STAR METHODS — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition
disease_details.notes: Also required seropositivity for rheumatoid factor and/or anti-citrullinated protein antibodies per ACR/EULAR 2010 criteria.

disease_response_orr.notes: Not a tumor/oncology ORR context; paper uses DAS28-based MTX-R/MTX-NR classification instead.

disease_response_pfs.notes: Not applicable; not an oncology study.

disease_response_recist.notes: Not applicable; no solid tumor response criteria used.

feces_phenotype.notes: Stool samples were extensively used, but no specific 'feces phenotype' clinical measurement (e.g., Bristol score) was reported.

fmt_id.evidence_quote: we colonized germ-free mice with a stool sample collected from a healthy human male (Donor 1
fmt_id.section: Results — Methotrexate has a broad impact on the human gut microbiota in gnotobiotic mice
fmt_id.notes: Additional donors (Donor 2 through 6) referenced throughout the Results and Methods sections for gnotobiotic colonization and ex vivo experiments.

fmt_role.evidence_quote: we colonized germ-free mice with a stool sample collected from a healthy human male (Donor 1
fmt_role.section: Results — Methotrexate has a broad impact on the human gut microbiota in gnotobiotic mice
fmt_role.notes: Human stool donors provided samples used to colonize germ-free/gnotobiotic mice (recipients); paper also references 'pre-MTX' and 'post-MTX' recipient mice groups but these describe mouse recipients, not human participant fmt_role status.

obgyn_pregnancy.notes: Not reported. Note: gnotobiotic mouse studies used female mice, but pregnancy status of human RA participants was not stated.

smoker.evidence_quote: more established risk factors like host genetics and smoking status
smoker.notes: Smoking is mentioned only as a general risk factor concept for future integration with microbiome data, not as an actual patient-level smoking status.

treatment.evidence_quote: Methotrexate (MTX), a first-line rheumatoid arthritis (RA) treatment, inhibits mammalian dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR)
treatment.notes: Patients received oral MTX at standard of care doses as prescribed by their treating rheumatologists (Methods).

tumor_staging_ajcc.notes: Not applicable; study is not oncology-focused.

tumor_staging_tnm.notes: Not applicable; study is not oncology-focused.

biomarker_name.evidence_quote: a decrease in DAS28 (Wells et al., 2009) of ≥1.8 and continued use of oral MTX
biomarker_name.section: Results — Clinical relevance of the interaction between methotrexate and the human gut microbiome
biomarker_name.notes: DAS28 is a disease activity score used to classify MTX responders (MTX-R) vs non-responders (MTX-NR); not a molecular biomarker but a clinical composite score reported quantitatively.

biomarker_unit.section: Results — Clinical relevance of the interaction between methotrexate and the human gut microbiome
biomarker_unit.notes: DAS28 is reported as a numeric score without an explicit unit label; 'score' inferred as the implicit unit.

value: baseline >2; decrease of ≥1.8 by month 4 defines responder
biomarker_value.evidence_quote: DAS28 score was greater than 2 at baseline and improved by at least 1.8 by month 4 post-treatment
biomarker_value.section: Methods — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition
biomarker_value.notes: Used to define MTX-R (responder) classification criteria.

disease_response_os.notes: No overall survival data reported; study focuses on microbiome and immune outcomes, not survival.

ecog_performance_status.notes: ECOG performance status not applicable/reported; this is a rheumatoid arthritis and microbiome study, not an oncology performance-status study.

feces_phenotype_value.notes: No discrete 'feces_phenotype' variable/measurement explicitly reported under this label; extensive microbiota composition data exist but not framed as a single phenotype value field.

tumor_size_measurement.notes: No tumor measurements reported; study concerns rheumatoid arthritis and gut microbiota, not oncology.

uncurated_metadata.notes: No additional free-text metadata identified that maps clearly to this generic field beyond what is already captured.

host_species.evidence_quote: New-onset RA was defined as disease duration of a minimum of 6 weeks and up to 6 months since diagnosis
host_species.section: STAR METHODS — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition
host_species.notes: The study involves human RA patients (fecal/microbiome sampling) as well as gnotobiotic (germ-free) mice colonized with human-derived stool; the human participant host species is Homo sapiens. Mice (Mus musculus, C57BL/6J) were used as experimental hosts for transplanted human microbiota but are not the 'participants' per se.

Multiple distinct human cohorts are described (healthy Donor 1, treatment-naive RA Donors 2/3, ex vivo Donors 4-6, 30 MTX-naive patients, NORA cohort n=23/n=17, MTX-R n=8 vs MTX-NR n=15) with different metadata reported for each; a single study-level value often does not represent all subgroups equally.
DNA extraction kit and sequencing platform differ between sample types (16S vs shotgun, human vs mouse); only the NYU human RA cohort values were extracted as most relevant to schema intent.
pmid field left not_reported because the PubMed ID is not stated within the paper's own text (only provided as external paper_id metadata).

This paper primarily studies rheumatoid arthritis patients and gnotobiotic mouse models; most fields in the schema (zygosity, neonatal, obgyn, tumor staging, HLA) are not relevant/reported in this context.

Human RA patient demographic details (specific ages, BMI, smoking status) beyond inclusion/exclusion criteria are not reported in the main text; may be present in supplementary Table S1A/S1C which was not provided in full.
fmt_role and fmt_id fields reflect human stool donors used for mouse colonization experiments; the paper does not provide a clean human-participant-level FMT recipient/donor table.
antibiotics_current_use and dietary_restriction were derived from exclusion criteria rather than directly stated positive values for enrolled patients; confidence lowered accordingly.

This paper is primarily a mechanistic/experimental study (microbiome, gnotobiotic mice, in vitro isolates) rather than a clinical oncology or biomarker-focused trial; most schema fields (tumor size, ECOG, OS, generic biomarker value/unit) are not applicable or not reported.

The 'biomarker' fields were populated using DAS28, a rheumatoid arthritis disease activity score, as the closest match to a quantifiable clinical indicator; this may not fit the intended scope of 'biomarker' in the schema and should be reviewed.

host_species field required a single value though both human (RA patients, stool donors) and mouse (gnotobiotic recipients) are used; 'human' was chosen as the primary participant species providing biological samples/data underlying most reported measurements.
